title: Verizon renews LaLiga sponsorship amid World Cup years
article_text:
Seven years after first signing on as a regional sponsor of LaLiga in the US and Canada, Verizon is renewing the deal under another multiyear agreement, the Spanish pro soccer league shared exclusively with Marketing Brew.

It’s the second time Verizon has re-upped its LaLiga sponsorship that began in the 2019-20 season, after first renewing it in 2023. The announcement comes sandwiched between two World Cups, with the men’s tournament held this past summer in North America, and the women’s coming up in Brazil next year.

With soccer fandom making strides in the US following the World Cup, Verizon has looked to stake its claim in the sport in a way that could help the brand stand out among other sponsors. In addition to serving as the official wireless telecommunications partner of LaLiga in the US and Canada, Verizon is hosting sweepstakes that provide fans access to the league, a sponsorship strategy the brand has carried over from its NFL and World Cup work.

For LaLiga, brands that want to activate experientially as opposed to just through official marks or media buys can help support the mission of growing fandom around the world, Nicolás García Hemme, managing director of LaLiga North America, told Marketing Brew.

“We go to market together, and the fans feel that the brand is very much there with LaLiga,” Hemme said. “It’s not just LaLiga delivering a logo.”

The latest deal focuses on the brand’s Verizon Shine loyalty program, which offers sweepstakes and merch drops through its app that include experiences with LaLiga like trips to Spain and meet and greets with legends from the league.

“Extending our long-standing partnership with LaLiga allows us to meaningfully fuel soccer fandom as momentum continues to surge,” Justin Toman, Verizon’s VP of partnerships, said in an email.

One complication to growing fandom is that soccer is a fragmented sport, Hemme said, and not just in terms of media rights.

“When you talk about basketball, you have the NBA,” he said. “When you talk about American football, you have the NFL. Then you talk soccer, and you have local soccer with MLS and the NWSL, then you have Liga MX, a huge deal here in the US due to the Hispanic population, and you have all the European soccer competition coming to the market.”

To stand out to sponsors in the US—which also include Walmart and Lowe’s—Hemme said his team leans into a few selling points of LaLiga, including some of its teams with rabid global fandom like Real Madrid and FC Barcelona, as well as the league’s connection with various Hispanic communities.

LaLiga’s growing audience in the US certainly doesn’t hurt among brands, either. The league had record US viewership across ESPN platforms for its 2025-26 season with more than 20 million viewers, up 10% YoY.

After the World Cup, Barcelona and Elche CF opened the 2026-27 season with 1 million viewers on ESPN platforms, making it the most-watched English-language match for LaLiga on the network. El Clásico, the iconic matchup between Barcelona and Real Madrid, averaged 2.4 million viewers on ABC and ESPN Deportes last month, up more than 50% from last season to become the most-watched LaLiga match for ESPN.

The involvement of sponsors like Verizon help support LaLiga’s efforts to grow that fandom even further, especially as the league looks to build its reputation among people outside of its core audience of Hispanic fans, Hemme said.

“For these [new] audiences,” he said, “you have to find other angles” to build affinity, including the more lifestyle-oriented experiences.

title: Leicester City terminate shirt sponsorship after adult film star backlash
article_text:
There was a time when Leicester City could do no wrong.

The Foxes went from one of the greatest underdog stories in sporting history to FA Cup winners, capturing the imagination of football supporters around the world. Today, however, the club find themselves fighting a very different battle, with financial troubles, successive relegations and a series of controversies threatening to tarnish their remarkable legacy.

Their latest scandal, involving a betting sponsor and an adult film performer, is perhaps another indication of just how difficult it has been for the club to find stability.

Few will ever forget their remarkable and awe-inspiring English Premier League championship run that had the entire world rooting for them during the 2015/16 season. As recently as 2021, the Foxes lifted the FA Cup.

Since those heady days, though, the club has been mired in controversy and a fall from grace that will be noted in the history books for years to come, with that cup triumph one of the few bright spots.

In 2025, the club was relegated from the elite division to the Championship, and a year later they dropped down again to League One. Currently, they are 11th in the third tier, having won only five of their 14 matches thus far.

Financial mismanagement, a carousel of managers and breaches of league financial rules have plagued the club since their famous title-winning campaign. But their latest controversy has further undermined their standing.

As reported by several media outlets, including the BBC, Leicester's main shirt sponsor, BC.GAME, parted ways with the club this week following a backlash over the betting company's appointment of Russian adult film performer Eva Elfie as their brand ambassador. Setting aside Elfie's appointment, with the company justifying her appointment due to her reach within the eSports and gaming communities, the BC.GAME sponsorship had been heavily questioned since its announcement in 2024, given that the company is an unlicensed gambling company in the UK.

In response to the Elfie announcement, the Foxes Trust — who are the official supporters' club of the team — said in a statement this week: "Both gambling and pornography can have devastating impacts on people's lives, in particular young people.

"Partnerships like these bring these two worlds to a larger audience and, by association, link them to Leicester City. Is this who we are now?"

In response, the club issued a statement on Wednesday confirming that the sponsorship had been terminated by "mutual consent" with immediate effect. They also announced a returns policy for supporters who had bought shirts bearing the BC.GAME branding through official club channels within the previous 28 days.

"Since the partnership was announced in 2024, the trust has consistently made clear that BC Game, for numerous reasons, does not reflect the values of our club or its supporters," the Foxes Trust said, after the sponsorship was terminated.

"That view has been shared by the great majority of fans who responded to our surveys. The recent partnership with an adult content creator only deepened those concerns and the trust felt the need to once again speak out publicly.

"This statement gained strong traction, emphasising the weight of feeling on this matter. Although we believe that the club should never have gone into partnership with BC Game, we nevertheless welcome this decision to part ways."

title: World Cup halo, Netflix and LA28: Can the NWSL capitalise on its once-in-a-generation opportunity?
article_text:
American sporting exceptionalism has long defined the country’s relationship with men’s soccer.

The world’s most popular sport has traditionally struggled to gain a foothold in a market where American football is king and baseball is woven into the national identity. The 1994 men’s Fifa World Cup catalysed the creation of Major League Soccer (MLS), but the tournament’s legacy was slow-burning, and a men’s national team that never threatened the latter stages of major competition prevented the sport from being thrust into the limelight.

Indeed, many still regarded soccer as a “foreign” pursuit best played by women and children. But it was precisely this attitude that created opportunities for female athletes at college level and on the global stage.

The US women’s national team are one of the dominant forces in the international game, and their victory in the 1999 Fifa Women’s World Cup delivered American soccer’s most iconic moment. The image of Brandi Chastain removing her shirt in celebration adorned the front page of national newspapersy, catapulting the sport into the mainstream.

The triumph renewed calls for greater investment in women’s soccer, setting in motion nearly three decades of growth (with a few hiccups along the way) that have coincided with rising popularity of the sport in general.

MLS is now firmly established, coverage of foreign competitions has gone from the periphery of sports media onto network television, and the 2026 men’s World Cup in North America was a national event in a way that USA 94 was not.

According to Nielsen, the number of people in the US identifying as soccer fans jumped from 66.8 million in July 2025 to 75.2 million in July 2026. Over the past five years, the growth rate has been 26 per cent.

Now, women’s soccer is ready to take up the baton and build on that momentum for sport’s entire ecosystem in the US. Next year’s Women’s World Cup in Brazil kicks off a four-year cycle that includes a new National Women’s Soccer League (NWSL) broadcast deal, further expansion, the Los Angeles 2028 Olympic Games, and the 2031 Women’s World Cup in North America.

“I’ve always wondered when Americans are going to begin to pay attention to this sport of soccer that the rest of the world is enjoying,” NWSL commissioner Jessica Berman told the Leaders Week sports business conference in London.

“But the [appreciation for the] culture around the game, the respect for the game [and] the appreciation for the unique attributes of the game that we had in America around the World Cup gave me a lot of enthusiasm and excitement about the future.”

Along with the Women’s National Basketball Association (WNBA), the NWSL is the most high-profile professional women’s team competition in the US. Now in its 14th season, the league’s business is booming by almost every measure. Match attendances, TV viewership and franchise valuations have all climbed considerably in recent years amid growing fan and investor interest.

Commercial rights values have never been higher, while a historic collective bargaining agreement (CBA), agreed in 2024 and running until 2030, delivered better pay and working conditions for players.

Average attendances rose by ten per cent during the first half of the 2026 campaign, while a game between Denver Summit and the Washington Spirit drew 63,004 fans to Empower Field at Mile High, a record for both the league and US women’s professional sport. Earlier this month, Gotham FC raised US$100 million at a record US$350 million valuation, and the league itself hopes to expand to 32 teams in the future.

These metrics are crucial as the league and its partner IMG take the NWSL’s domestic broadcast rights to market. Next season is the last to be covered by four-year US$240 million pacts with CBS, ESPN, Amazon Prime Video and Scripps’ Ion.

The NWSL’s current media strategy is designed to cast the net as wide as possible at the expense of consolidation. CBS offers network coverage and a committed audience of soccer fans on Paramount+, ESPN is the most important sports platform in the country, Amazon Prime reaches streaming-first and younger viewers, and Ion has a growing portfolio of women’s sports rights.

Broadcast ratings for the 2026 regular season were a mixed bag. Viewership on ESPN was static and down ten per cent on CBS, while Roku stepped in as a fifth partner after the collapse of Victory+. But the deals have been successful from a revenue, discoverability and audience expansion perspective.

Berman will be confident that the league’s growing audience, broadcaster demand for live sport and the fees commanded by the WNBA will lead to another improved deal – not to mention rising interest in soccer following the World Cup. And, if nothing else, the addition of two new teams in 2028, when the new deals begin, will increase inventory.

“The next 12 months are going to be critically important and foundational for the next stage of growth for the NWSL,” Berman said. “Our biggest growth opportunity is continuing to build and scale audience.

“Our media deal had us really lean into the discoverability of our property. So, we have incredible partners in ESPN, CBS, Amazon and Ion [and Roku]. Our audience is really spread across multiple channels and so we’re really working hard to prioritise key matches and aggregate audience, so that we can really go into this next cycle continuing to build on the strength of the NWSL.”

The league is tight-lipped about whether it will continue with five partners. ESPN’s coverage of the final round of regular season matches, which saw it broadcast all eight games in a single window, showed the benefits of consolidation. The Disney-owned broadcaster has also scheduled some matches in primetime to fill the gap left by MLB, giving the league further reach and prominence.

title: "It was scary at 100km/h" - F1 drivers shocked by Las Vegas 'ice rink'
article_text:
With rain affecting Thursday's Las Vegas Grand Prix running on the low-grip street circuit around the Strip, the biggest takeaway was not who was fastest, but the impressive fact that every Formula 1 driver kept it out of the barriers.

Following F1's first proper wet weekend of the year in Brazil, using both the full wets and intermediates tyres in qualifying and race conditions, drivers were concerned over how Pirelli's wet weather range would work on a circuit without high-speed corners, where tyres are much harder to get up to temperature.

"I think the scary times are if you go to Vegas and you can't get any tyre temperature," McLaren's Lando Norris said after the Sao Paulo race, with Racing Bulls driver Liam Lawson adding: "If we're on a track like Vegas and it rains, honestly, I think we're in trouble."

Norris and Lawson didn't have to wait long for their predictions to be put to the test. Vegas only saw 22 days of rain in 2025, making rainfall affecting the grand prix a long shot. In a city obsessed by odds, it's the equivalent of hitting a split bet on two numbers at the any roulette tables lining the Strip.

That precipitation duly arrived in copious amounts, making Thursday's first practice session a complete wash, with no drivers even logging a lap time as most of the pack restricted itself to one exploration lap on full wet tyres, largely out of curiosity.

FP2 was more action-packed, starting on the full wets before moving to intermediates as a dry line started forming. The oily, grimy track lined with paint proved an 'ice rink', as Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad described his Vegas debut. Drivers particularly struggled on their first couple of laps of a stint as they wrangled their tyres into a reasonable temperature range.

"It did shock me," Lindblad said. "We've said many times that these tyres are not good. I think the drivers already complained last year that the wet tyres didn't work here. They weren't working on a lot of tracks we went to this year.

"But this was an experience I've never had before in a car. It was honestly scary to drive even at 100 km/h in a low-speed corner. Just four wheels sliding, not knowing if you're going into a wall. Obviously it doesn't help with all the paint and walls because it's a street track. It was a very new experience for me and honestly the closest I can relate to it was driving a rally car on ice versus Formula 1."

More experienced drivers backed up Lindblad's opinion, too. "Yeah, I'm always surprised when I see no crashes or nothing, because you feel like you have those moments a lot out there yourself," said Williams' Alex Albon. "But the trickiest track of the year, lowest grip of the year, these cars in a wet track, it's a lot of sliding."

After FP1, Pirelli decided to increase the tyre blanket temperature for its full wet tyres from 40C to 60C, which somewhat helped the initial warm-up, but Albon felt it didn't go far enough. "I think these tyres are too cold. I think we need hotter blankets. I don't know why we run so cold on the blankets, because we still use them, so it doesn't make a difference if we run them a bit hotter," he said.

McLaren's Oscar Piastri added: "Pretty impossible at the start. Even when we put the inters on, for the first couple of laps it was worse than the wet and a lot more tricky. So, definitely not easy out there."

Not everyone agreed, though, as Red Bull's Isack Hadjar actually said he quite enjoyed the intermediate running. "In FP1, it was very difficult. That's why we didn't really drive. And then FP2 was fairly easy," the Frenchman said.

"I think the extreme tyre was too extreme. The intermediate was working perfectly and it was good fun, honestly. I had good fun driving around."

Following early development work and a number of wet weather tyre tests, tyre supplier Pirellis is planning to introduce updated tyres as early as next season.

title: Pirelli reintroduces stint limit for F1 Qatar GP
article_text:
Formula 1 teams will again have to follow a prescribed stint limit for each car at the Qatar Grand Prix to protect the Pirelli tyres around the high-degradation track.

Drivers must complete no more than 27 laps per stint at Lusail International Circuit, meaning teams will likely opt for a two-stop strategy in the 57-lap race.

It is a similar situation to last year when stints were limited to 25 laps following analysis of the 2024 contest, where “several tyres, particularly the left front, had reached the maximum wear”. The 2023 event was also the subject of stint limits, though that year, the enforced limit was just 18 laps.

That came after teams attempted stints of over 30 laps, which is especially challenging at the 16-turn, 5.4km circuit that features various types of corners - particularly medium-to-high-speed.

Pirelli’s chief F1 engineer Simone Berra said at this weekend’s Las Vegas Grand Prix: “The same limitation in terms of rules, but the number of laps will be 27, not 25.

“We increased by two laps. We have seen from our indoor testing that this is, let's say, acceptable without any particular risk.

“But we know the issue in Qatar is that we have very high localised wear, especially on the front, with 100% wear easily reached after 25, 26 laps on average.

“This is generating higher stress on the tyre because you don't have the thread compound protecting the structure and then you have high loads, high lateral loads there, and high temperature, high carcass temperature.

“So, these are the factors that are influencing more the integrity resistance of the tyre.”

Every lap a driver completes during the race, including those behind a safety car, will count towards the total and a disqualification is the likely punishment for anybody who fails to oblige.

It doesn’t mean strategic options are limited though, as 2025 saw McLaren opt against pitting under a lap seven safety car to maintain flexibility and not have to stop again before lap 32.

Oscar Piastri and Lando Norris stayed out until the end of the stint limit, but this still backfired as it meant both drivers lost the victory to title rival Max Verstappen at Red Bull.

The grand prix ended as a predominantly two-stop contest nevertheless and it followed the 19-lap sprint race on the Saturday, which will not feature in this year’s event.

Berra added: “We are going to keep the same laps limitation just to induce the two stops and avoid any risk of running on the under-thread for multiple laps and generating integrity issues.

“We know that if you reach 100% wear on the front, then you don't really induce a big degradation.

“The teams, they can easily manage the front axle in the long runs, they don't stop if they don't see quite a significant drop in performance.

“So, that's the situation, and we will count the number of laps for each session. It will be a little bit easier because it's no more a sprint event this year, while it was last year.

“So, even the lap count will be easier for us and we will review the lap count and release the remaining laps per set at the end of Saturday running.”

Qatar will serve as the penultimate grand prix of the 23-round 2026 campaign with Abu Dhabi hosting the finale on 4-6 December.

title: Five drivers set for grid penalties for engine changes at F1 Las Vegas GP
article_text:
Five drivers will take grid penalties for the Las Vegas Grand Prix, including new Formula 1 world champion Kimi Antonelli.

As previously indicated by Mercedes, Antonelli will take a five-place grid drop for an internal combustion engine change – but does not pick up a further penalty for a turbocharger change due to still being within his allocation.

Mercedes announced the 2026 F1 world champion would take on its upgraded turbo specification as permitted under ADUO, while Russell would stick with the current specification due to needing to serve a greater grid penalty for exceeding his allocation.

McLaren’s Oscar Piastri will serve a 10-place grid penalty for an engine change – as previously indicated by the team – while Carlos Sainz will also serve a 10-place penalty after Williams opted to give him his fifth turbocharger of the season.

Like Antonelli, both Piastri and team-mate Lando Norris will be equipped with the upgraded Mercedes turbo.

Oliver Bearman will serve a back of the grid penalty for an almost entire power unit change – including his fifth internal combustion engine, fifth turbocharger, fifth exhaust and fifth MGU-K – which would tally up to 35 places in total.

Finally, Lance Stroll will take a ninth new energy store and an eight new control electronics in Las Vegas after his Honda-powered Aston Martin suffered its latest battery-related retirement last time out in Brazil. The Canadian will serve a 10-place grid penalty in total for the two changes.

title: Howden Takes Irish Champion Hurdle Title Sponsorship in Three-Year Deal
article_text:
Howden has signed a three-year deal with Leopardstown Racecourse and Horse Racing Ireland to become the title sponsor of the Irish Champion Hurdle at the Dublin Racing Festival.

The first running of the Howden Irish Champion Hurdle will take place on Sunday, January 31, 2027, the second day of the festival at Leopardstown. The Grade 1 race carries a €200,000 prize fund and counts Hatton’s Grace, Istabraq, Hurricane Fly, Honeysuckle and State Man among its past winners.

The agreement comes as the global insurance broker expands its Irish business. Howden has 30 local offices across the country, providing commercial and personal insurance, financial advice and mortgages.

Mark Nolan, CEO of Howden Ireland, said the sponsorship reflected the company’s commitment to “supporting not only the equine industry, but the wider network of businesses and communities connected to it, from transport and hospitality to the many other services that help the industry thrive.”

“We are thrilled to welcome Howden as the new title sponsor of the Irish Champion Hurdle, a race steeped in history and sporting excellence,” added Rob Crabbe, Commercial Manager at HRI Racecourses.

“The Dublin Racing Festival has grown into one of the most iconic weekends in jump racing, and the Champion Hurdle is its crowning jewel on day two. Partnering with a prestigious global brand like Howden for the next three years highlights the international appeal and commercial strength of Irish racing.”

“We look forward to working closely with the Howden team to deliver an exceptional event.”

There is a clear fit between the audience at Leopardstown and the businesses Howden is looking to reach through its Irish office network.

Nolan’s reference to transport and hospitality points to where the sponsorship could do some of its best work, linking together the different strands in an industry that is also a sport, and a sport which is also a substantial industry.

Three years gives its local teams time to build relationships with the businesses that keep racing going throughout the year.

title: Cadillac CEO Towriss on Herta’s future and Bottas’ extension
article_text:
With Cadillac opting to retain Valtteri Bottas for 2027 rather than promoting Colton Herta, CEO Dan Towriss has explained what the next steps might be for the American driver.

Cadillac CEO Dan Towriss has given an update on Colton Herta’s future after the American missed out on a potential F1 promotion in 2027, following the announcement that Valtteri Bottas will remain with the squad.

While Sergio Perez’s contract extension was confirmed ahead of the Mexico City Grand Prix in October, speculation persisted over whether Bottas would stay in the other seat or if Herta – who has acted as a test driver for the team this year – might be given the opportunity.

Alongside embarking on his debut F2 campaign in 2026, Herta has participated in six Free Practice 1 outings for Cadillac – meaning that he accumulated enough Super Licence points to allow him to race in F1.

However, the American outfit ultimately decided to retain Bottas for 2027, a decision that Towriss reiterated was “right” for them as he spoke to the media on Thursday at the Las Vegas Grand Prix.

When asked if there was ever any doubt over Bottas’ position, Towriss responded: “We did want to take a look at it. I think as we look across the races, while [his pace in] practice and Qualifying was similar to Checo, race pace was down.

“Some of that [involves] things behind the scenes that are out of Valtteri's control. We did want to take a look at that. We were working hard to get Colton Herta ready as well.

“It's important to have an American driver for our team with our team, racing, but ultimately, when we took a look at it, Valtteri's the right guy.

“We want to keep Checo and Valtteri together, their experience, the continuity, what they bring to the team. Ultimately it was the right decision for the team and we were happy to extend Valtteri. He's been absolutely fantastic for us.”

In terms of what this means for Herta’s next steps, Towriss explained that there are “a number of options on the table” for the 26-year-old.

“We've offered him a reserve position,” the American said. “The seat's open for ’28, so there are options on the table for Colton. There are options in other sports as well. I think he's decided on a direction, but we're still in conversations on that and look forward to seeing what Colton wants to do.”

Towriss acknowledged that Herta was “disappointed” by the decision and went on to praise the former IndyCar racer for taking on the challenge of the past year.

“It was definitely a tough decision – a tough discussion with Colton,” he explained. “I think he was disappointed. There was a lot of work, a lot of a build-up [to] go into this. I know Colton was very brave in even taking on this risk, going into F2 and trying to cram all this learning in.

“I think it was obvious it was a very tough season for Colton in F2 this year, but I think the work that he did in FP1s and the TPC [Testing of Previous Cars] setting [was] quite strong and showed that he really is capable of driving this car. But when we look at where the team is right now and what's needed for the team, Valtteri was the best decision going forward.

“But we're going to continue to talk to Colton about the options that are on the table and give it a little bit of time, because I think he is disappointed to not have that opportunity. So much went into this, but he's just a tremendous talent and we're excited about what's ahead for him.”

title: Zak Brown explains why McLaren keeps selling F1 cars before they race ahead of 2027 auction
article_text:
For McLaren fans. Papaya news from Woking, with the latest on the drivers, the car, team strategy and every race weekend.

McLaren Racing CEO Zak Brown has explained why the Woking outfit is selling its Formula 1 cars at auction before they have even turned a wheel, saying the alternative is leaving them hidden away.

McLaren will auction its 2027 car, the MCL41, with RM Sotheby's in Abu Dhabi on 9 December, three days after the season finale. A chassis used by either Lando Norris or Oscar Piastri will be offered with a 2027-specification Mercedes power unit.

It follows last year's sale of this season's car, the MCL40A, which went for a staggering $11.48million at RM Sotheby's Abu Dhabi sale last December. It was the first time an F1 car had been sold before it had raced.

The buyer will not receive that car until 2028, because of rules designed to stop rivals getting access to a team's intellectual property, and was offered a 2025 show car to display in the meantime.

Asked in the team principals' press conference in Las Vegas about the thinking behind the sales, Brown said it made more sense than locking the cars away.

"Yeah, the other alternative is you leave them all on shelves under wraps, which is a shame. We have a great automotive business, we have a very passionate fan base, and we have a certain part of our fan base that has a passion to collect cars," Brown said.

Brown, a keen car collector himself, said last year's buyer had been able to follow their car all season.

"And so last year with Sotheby's, we sold '26 cars and someone had the ability to come on the journey, watch their car race, win some races. And so we're going to do that once a year at least. That's our intention," he said.

McLaren's 2026 car has won three races this season, all with Norris, in Hungary, the Netherlands and Brazil. The team currently sits fourth in the constructors' championship with 398 points, 17 points behind Red Bull in third.

This year's winning bidder will get a tour of McLaren's Woking headquarters before the 2027 season, the chance to meet Brown, Norris and Piastri, and an invitation to the team's 2027 launch.

Brown said the sales gave a small group of fans an experience that would otherwise not exist.

"We have a nice business. We've done 35 track cars of our Le Mans car, so for us it's about experiential opportunities for those fans of ours that are in a privileged position to be able to own Formula 1 cars. Otherwise, we make four or five cars a year and they end up stacking up on a shelf, and that's no good for anybody," he said.

title: Chairwoman of Bundestag's Sports Committee to QNA: Qatar Enhanced its Status as a Global Sports Hub
article_text:
Berlin, November 20 (QNA) - Chairwoman of the Committee on Sports and Volunteering of the German Bundestag Aydan Ozoguz, who is also a Member of the Foreign Affairs Committee, affirmed that the State of Qatar has demonstrated its ability to host major sporting events of global significance, praising the efforts made over recent years to establish the country as a global sports hub.

In exclusive remarks to Qatar News Agency (QNA), Ozoguz said that Qatar's hosting of the FIFA World Cup Qatar 2022 had demonstrated its ability to provide the organisational requirements, infrastructure and extensive technical capabilities necessary to stage a sporting event of such magnitude and global importance.

She stressed that there was considerable scope for expanding Qatari-German cooperation in sports, the exchange of expertise, the development of young talent, volunteering and parliamentary diplomacy. Ozoguz added that the State of Qatar had made significant efforts over recent years to strengthen its presence on the international sporting stage, noting that one aspect deserving particular attention was how to make long-term use of the expertise gained from organising major sporting tournaments and events.

The Chairwoman of the Bundestag's Committee on Sports and Volunteering noted that the sports facilities, training centres and sports medicine facilities developed by Qatar offered opportunities and benefits extending beyond the hosting of individual international events, as these facilities would continue to serve sports and society, particularly young people, on a sustainable basis.

Ozoguz outlined several areas of potential cooperation between Qatar and Germany in the sporting field, highlighting opportunities to benefit from Germany's contributions and expertise in the sports club system, the development of emerging talent and support for athletes pursuing dual careers that combine sporting activities with education or vocational training.

She also pointed to Germany's experience in organising grassroots and elite sports, stressing the importance of mutual support between the two countries in achieving their shared objectives.

Regarding the role of sports in strengthening Qatari-German relations, the Bundestag committee chairwoman affirmed that sports possessed a unique ability to bring people closer together and transcend geographical, linguistic, cultural and even political boundaries.

She noted that sporting activities created opportunities for people to meet and communicate beyond the traditional frameworks of political and economic relations. She also noted that sports constituted an important pillar of relations between Qatar and Germany, not only at the level of official institutions but also among male and female athletes and the peoples of both countries. She added that sports could help strengthen existing connections between sporting federations, clubs, universities and non-governmental organisations, opening broader avenues for institutional and community-level cooperation.

She also emphasised the role of Qatari-German cooperation in creating greater opportunities for young people in both countries to participate in joint programmes and initiatives, considering that open exchanges among young people could help build trust and enhance mutual understanding among all parties.

Regarding the prospects for international cooperation and the exchange of expertise, Ozoguz said that her participation in parliamentary discussions with international sports organisations and federations had reinforced her conviction that sporting issues could no longer be addressed in isolation from political developments and international relations.

She said that the belief that sports and politics could be completely separated did not reflect reality, as the two fields were interconnected in numerous ways. She added that constructive and positive cooperation between countries could reduce the likelihood of this interaction between politics and sports producing negative consequences or developments that could damage the reputation of sports.

The Chairwoman of the Committee on Sports and Volunteering of the German Bundestag, explained in remarks to Qatar News Agency (QNA) that organising sporting events, supporting male and female athletes, and developing modern facilities could no longer be viewed from a purely national perspective, making international cooperation and the exchange of knowledge and expertise indispensable.

She affirmed that Qatar and Germany had opportunities to expand their cooperation in this field, both at the level of sports policies and through the exchange of expertise and knowledge among sports federations and organising committees of major tournaments and events.

Ozoguz expressed her hope for intensified communication and exchanges between the two countries' parliamentarians, universities and sports federations, allowing both sides to benefit from each other's experiences and expertise.

Regarding volunteering, Ozoguz told QNA that voluntary work constituted one of the fundamental pillars of German society, noting that approximately 27 million people in Germany participated in volunteer activities, representing around 37 percent of the population aged 14 and above.

She proposed several ideas for Qatari-German cooperation in volunteering, including the possibility of developing joint programmes for young people and volunteers in both countries, enabling them to meet and exchange experiences through participation in sporting events, club activities and social projects. She added that such initiatives could provide direct opportunities for interaction among young people and strengthen human and community ties between the two countries.

Ozoguz added that volunteering encompassed a wide range of activities, including disaster protection, sports club activities, childcare and youth support, sports coaching and refereeing, and participation in organising activities and managing the day-to-day operations of clubs.

She stressed that without the contributions of these volunteers, German sports would not have achieved their current breadth and diversity. She affirmed that appreciation for voluntary work should not be limited to verbal praise but should be accompanied by appropriate organisational conditions, reduced bureaucratic procedures while maintaining necessary oversight, sustained support and greater public recognition of the value of volunteer contributions. She noted that individuals who assumed voluntary responsibilities deserved appropriate recognition and appreciation from society for their efforts.

title: Hot Wheels ‘Tiniest Team Principal’ search opens
article_text:
A global competition to identify three young F1 fans for an official Hot Wheels role and VIP access to a Grand Prix is underway.

Mattel has announced a global search for the first-ever Hot Wheels ‘Tiniest Team Principal’, with one winner to be selected from each of the United States, the United Kingdom, and Mexico.

The winners will also be flown, with their families, to Hot Wheels headquarters in El Segundo, California, where they will meet the design and executive teams behind Hot Wheels and Formula 1, and take part in picking and designing their own Hot Wheels F1 die-cast car.

Each ‘Tiniest Team Principal’ will step into an official ambassador role for the Hot Wheels brand and receive VIP access to a Formula 1 Grand Prix.

The entry period is open now and will run through June 16. Parents or legal guardians of children aged five to ten can submit an entry video on TikTok or Instagram, with official rules available here. Winners will be announced on June 23

Submissions can include custom trackset builds, race predictions, original designs, or a passionate explanation of how they would run an F1 team.

Entries will be reviewed by a judging panel that includes Formula 1 President and CEO Stefano Domenicali, 2009 FIA Formula One World Drivers’ Champion and F1 Ambassador Jenson Button, Mattel’s General Manager and Head of Vehicles and Building Sets Ted Wu, and Hot Wheels designer Kristina Albrecht.

Stefano Domenicali, President and CEO of Formula 1, said: “In Formula 1, you must be ready to make the big decisions when it matters most. This is a fantastic way to put our youngest fans right at the heart of the action, giving them a unique chance to go behind the scenes for a once-in-a-lifetime experience.

"I’m really looking forward to seeing this evolution of this partnership and the incredible creativity and passion they bring to running their own team… I think some of our current Team Principals might even need to watch out!”

Jenson Button, 2009 FIA Formula One World Drivers’ Champion, added: “In Formula 1, the difference between winning and losing can come down to one decision. Kids make those kinds of calls every time they play with Hot Wheels. I know the Hot Wheels Tiniest Team Principal will keep the rest of the paddock on their toes.”

Ted Wu, General Manager and Global Head of Vehicles and Building Sets at Mattel said: “The task is simple. We are looking for someone who builds, rebuilds, and takes on every challenge. A kid with strong opinions on what makes a car faster, cooler, and more fun. The Tiniest Team Principal might even take my job for the day… as long as I get it back.”

For official rules, submission guidelines, and eligibility requirements, visit mattel.com/hot-wheels-f1.
